- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.00), model overpredicts; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast.
- Model overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; reduce first 3–5 days’ forecast by 1–1.5%.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.00) triggers model lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce slope of decline.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, apply correction based on sentiment direction: + if bullish, - if bearish.
